answer.reason: Libnah has two defining events in the verses: its capture by Joshua and its revolt from Judah under Joram.

clauses.english: was taken by Joshua, who smote it with the sword, the LORD delivering it and its king into Israel's hand
clauses.quote: the LORD delivered it also, and the king thereof, into the hand of Israel

clauses.english: revolted from Judah at the time Edom revolted
clauses.quote: Then Libnah revolted at the same time.

doubts: The first clause is somewhat long; it may be trimmed to "was taken by Joshua and its people and king were smitten with the sword".
JOS 12:15, 2KI 19:8, ISA 37:8 (the king of Assyria warring against Libnah) and the mentions of Jeremiah of Libnah were left out as list entries, a passing detail, or a relation to another person.
